concepts.preferred_label: Dextrocardia with complete right bundle branch block
concepts.why: The patient's ECG showed a wide QRS complex with right bundle branch block morphology and the imaging revealed the heart's apex directed to the right, indicating dextrocardia with complete right bundle branch block.
The patient's physical examination and imaging revealed the apex of the heart located at the right side of the chest and hepatic dullness in the left subcostal region, indicating situs inversus.
The patient's ECG showed a wide QRS complex with right bundle branch block morphology, indicating right bundle branch block.
The patient's imaging revealed the heart's apex directed to the right, indicating cardiac malposition.

concepts.preferred_label: Corrected Transposition of the Great Arteries
concepts.why: The combination of negative P waves with pathological Q waves in leads I and aVL, positive P waves in lead V1, and biphasic P waves in leads V2 through V6 explains the unusual cardiac anatomy.

rationales.F11: The echocardiogram showing the right atrium and ventricle on the left and the left atrium and ventricle on the right with the apex directed to the right is diagnostic of dextrocardia.
rationales.F12: The corrected ECG showing normal sinus rhythm with complete right bundle branch block supports the diagnosis of dextrocardia with complete right bundle branch block.
